lots.guide_summary: All evidence is SOLD hammer at Gowans, Hobart, in AUD (no FX). Close 9ct gold and pearl pairs made $60, $70, $110 and $220 between Oct 2025 and Aug 2026; category guides $35-$45. No UNSOLD or ASKING entries survive or were found. Melt reference only (not a sale): gold USD 4184/oz (gold-api.com, 2026-10-16) x 1.447 USD/AUD (frankfurter.app, 2026-10-15) = about A$194.6/g fine, A$113.9/g at 14ct.
lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving close SOLD in the last 24 months = $60 (Gowans 368497, Oct 2025). $60 / 1.22 = $49.18, round down to $45. Flip: likely resale about $110 (middle of the $60-$220 close sales); less about 15% seller commission ($16.50) and $10 outbound postage = $83.50; / 2.44 = $34.22, round down to $30. Inbound freight $0 (pickup at Invermay). If the 14ct mark and a weight of 1.5g+ of gold are confirmed, melt alone would justify more, but no SOLD 14ct pearl pair supports a higher figure yet.

lots.key_photo_findings: One photo only. Two round white pearls about 6-7mm with good lustre and no visible blemishes, in yellow scroll-and-leaf open frames with hinged hook/lever fittings. Enlarged crop shows no readable stamp; the backs and fittings are not shown.
lots.condition: Looks good, pearls bright with no visible chips or peeling; fittings appear intact from the front. Backs not seen.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you confirm a 14ct (585) stamp on the fittings, give the total weight in grams, and confirm both hinged fittings close properly and the pearls are firm in their settings?

lots.what_it_is: Fourteen Australian florins in a card tray (the researcher said about 15; I count 7 per row). Readable: 1961, two 1947, two 1901-1951 Jubilee florins, a later date in the 1950s, at least one older 'FLORIN' shield type (1910-1936 design, .925 silver) and several heavily worn pieces. Most look like post-1946 .500 silver.
lots.score_reason: Silver florins are a melt-driven commodity at present: silver USD 57.86/oz (gold-api.com, 2026-10-16) x 1.447 USD/AUD = about A$2.69/g, so a .500 florin holds about A$15.20 of silver and a .925 florin about A$28.20. Fourteen coins are worth about A$215-$240 in melt, and Gowans florin parcels sell at about $16-$21 a coin hammer, in line with that. No key dates seen.

lots.working: Keep: lowest per-coin close SOLD in the last 24 months is Gowans 408019, $190 / 12 = $15.83 a coin; x 14 coins = $221.67; / 1.22 = $181.69, round down to $180 (all-in $219.60, about melt). Selling to a bullion buyer at about 90% of melt (about A$195-$215) gives a similar figure. Inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Several dates read in enlarged crops (1947 x2, 1951 Jubilee x2, 1961) and five close Gowans SOLD florin parcels opened with photos checked; values agree with the melt calculation. Exact number of .925 pieces is uncertain but moves the value only by about $25.
lots.key_photo_findings: Fourteen coins, two rows of seven. Dates read: 1961, 1947 (two), 1901-1951 Jubilee (two), one 1950s date. Top right coin shows the older 'FLORIN' shield reverse (1910-1936, .925). One top row coin is worn almost smooth and one has toning. No 1927 Canberra, 1934-35 Centenary or 1932 seen.
lots.condition: Circulated, Fine to Very Fine, some heavily worn and one toned. Bullion grade, not collector grade.
lots.question_for_armitage: How many florins are in the lot and are there any not shown in the photo? If convenient, the total weight in grams would confirm the silver content.
